text:
nik: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I want to lock down the demarcation between SLA-weighted scaling and ordinary burst admission. TL;DR: propose a thin controller that enforces SLA-weight bands and hands off to the existing autoscaler for capacity changes.

maria: thin controller = admission gate + accounting, right? not another scaler? :thinking_face:

sam: +1 on not adding another control loop. can we express SLA weight as a token-bucket parameter per-tenant? that keeps the runtime simple.

lee: token-bucket sounds fine but we need deterministic degrade behavior. if SLA band is exhausted, do we fallback to lower-latency model variant or rate-limit requests? both have UX impacts.

nik: idea: SLA bands are prioritized tokens. Two actions when band exhausted: 1) admission rejection (soft throttling) 2) automated variant fallback if tenant opted in. Config looks like:

```
# per-tenant policy
sla_weight: 0.8
token_bucket:
  capacity: 1000
  refill_per_min: 500
fallback_order:
  - model: gptx-small-8q
  - model: gptx-2b-int8
```

maria: that config is readable. we should also track perceived p95 latency and factor that into refill rate (adaptive refill). otherwise burst patterns will either starve or overshoot.

sam: adaptive refill makes sense but be careful with oscillation. keep a smoothing window and a min refill floor. maybe EWMA over 60s.

lee: also need an operator-visible signal: "sla_band_depleted" events + metric tags so SREs can build alerts. otherwise ops will be blind.

infra-bot: deploy status: autoscaler-proxy v0.9 deployed to canary (cluster-b). no rollbacks.

nik: ops signal + metrics planned. open questions: where to run the thin controller? options: a) colocated admission webhook in operator b) central proxy in control plane c) runtime-side admission inside the runtime process.

maria: pros/cons: webhook = simple for policy mutation but adds latency; control-plane proxy = single place to reason but needs HA; runtime-side = fastest but harder to ship policy changes.

sam: leaning control-plane proxy. can implement gradual rollout and simulate decisions with a dry-run mode. also easier to generate events and audit logs.

lee: policy testing idea: we should add a simulation harness that replays recent traffic and runs admission decisions offline to estimate P95 and cost delta per tenant. small script + job.

nik: agree. I'll sketch a sim job that uses a day's worth of traces and evaluates: admission_rejections, fallback_invocations, extra_tokens_consumed, cost_delta. will output CSV.

maria: implementation nit: keep policy evaluation pure and side-effect free so dry-run is exact. store decisions and metrics separately.

sam: rollout plan draft: (1) implement policy evaluator + dry-run, (2) ship control-plane proxy in canary with dry-run enabled for 1 week, (3) enable enforcement for <5 tenants, (4) expand to more tenants + add fallback variants.

lee: one more tradeoff: rate-limiting vs rejection with retry-after header. Many clients will retry aggressively and push the problem. we should return structured error with suggested backoff and a link to tenant console to opt-in fallback.

nik: good call. include `Retry-After` and `X-Redwood-Fallback-URL` in the error payload when appropriate. also surface per-tenant SLA burn-rate dashboard in Console.

maria: sounds like a plan. who will own the sim harness? I can take the first pass this week.

sam: I'll prototype the control-plane proxy interface and a policy YAML schema.

lee: I'll wire up metrics and the error payload semantics.

nik: awesome. logging decision: keep a single audit stream for policy decisions (json lines) and forward to kafka topic `sla-policy-decisions.v1`. infra-bot already approved topic.

infra-bot: notice: topic `sla-policy-decisions.v1` created with retention 14d.

nik: ok closing — follow-ups: maria sim PR, sam proxy sketch, lee metrics + error format. please post PR links here when ready. thanks all :raised_hands:
